verdict.rationale: LiteLLM documents a formal API Stability Policy that defines public endpoints as those in the OpenAPI spec and calls out breaking changes in release notes. A Release Cycle page adds semantic versioning, with major bumps reserved for backward-incompatible changes and a recommendation to pin to stable 1.x.x. Together these form a documented versioning-and-deprecation contract, though the deprecation mechanics are thin. Missing for 10: explicit deprecation notice periods or sunset timelines for endpoints, per-endpoint API versioning beyond package semver, independent or hands-on corroboration that the policy is honored.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: Every endpoint that appears in the proxy's OpenAPI spec is public
Breaking changes are called out in a dedicated section of the release notes.
Together with the API Stability Policy this is the documented versioning-and-deprecation contract.
